name: Project Fennel
one_liner: A SaaS platform that connects to existing scanners, DevOps and IT tools to prioritise vulnerabilities and orchestrate their remediation end to end.

buyer.role: CISO or CIO; vulnerability management program owner
buyer.company_profile: Mid-size and large enterprises (1,000+ staff) running several vulnerability scanners and code-testing tools with thousands of open findings and slow patching.

user: Vulnerability management analysts, IT operations and DevOps engineers who apply fixes.

problem.summary: Scanners find far more vulnerabilities than teams can fix, and it often takes weeks or months before a patch rolls out. Known flaws are exploited in high-profile breaches. Detection is crowded, but remediation, coordinating teams, tasks and tools to actually fix issues, is manual work in spreadsheets and tickets.

evidence.claim: A major breach exploited a known web-framework vulnerability months after a patch was available.
Vulnerability management covers identifying, prioritising and remediating vulnerabilities, with remediation the slowest stage.
Patches must be tested and deployed across many systems, which delays remediation.
Thousands of new CVEs are published every year.

why_now.summary: Software is adopted and shipped faster, increasing exposure, while DevOps and IT tools (configuration management, CI, ticketing) now expose APIs that make automated remediation feasible.

features.feature: Agentless API connectors to vulnerability scanners, code-testing tools, cloud, CMDB and ticketing
features.why: Use the data customers already have; no network taps.

features.feature: Prioritisation using business, DevOps and IT context in addition to threat intelligence
Remediation database of patches, scripts and workarounds per vulnerability
features.why: Tells teams exactly how to fix.

features.feature: Orchestration engine that creates, routes and tracks remediation tasks and can push fixes via Puppet/Chef/Ansible

features.why: Proves the fix and shows risk reduction to CIOs/CISOs.

competitors.name: Kenna Security
competitors.how_we_differ: Goes beyond risk scoring to orchestrate and validate the fix.

competitors.name: RiskSense
competitors.how_we_differ: Uses DevOps and IT data and a remediation database, not only threat-based prioritisation.

competitors.name: ServiceNow Vulnerability Response
competitors.how_we_differ: Vendor-neutral remediation intelligence rather than a workflow on a CMDB.

competitors.name: Qualys
competitors.how_we_differ: Aggregates many scanners and code tools instead of one vendor's findings.

differentiation: Focuses on the remediation gap rather than detection: agentless, works over existing tools' APIs, prioritises with business and DevOps context, and drives fixes to closure with a curated remediation database.

build.team: About 15 people: R&D in Israel plus US sales and support, founders from elite military cyber units
hardest_parts: Building a remediation database at scale
Getting IT and DevOps teams to accept automated changes

pricing.model: Annual SaaS subscription per asset under management
pricing.entry_price: Working assumption: $30,000/year for up to 2,500 assets
pricing.rationale: Priced against analyst time saved and scanner spend.

comparables.price: No public list price at the time (quote-based enterprise sale)
No public list price at the time (quote-based enterprise sale)

go_to_market.first_customers: Ten US and Israeli enterprises with multiple scanners, a dedicated vulnerability management lead and an audit finding about patch latency.
go_to_market.channel: Direct sales to CISOs/CIOs with beta access for qualified customers; partnerships with scanner vendors.
go_to_market.wedge: Connect existing scanners and show a prioritised, deduplicated remediation plan within a day.

risks: Remediation database is hard to maintain

riskiest_assumption.assumption: Enterprises will pay a separate vendor for remediation orchestration on top of scanners and ITSM.
riskiest_assumption.test: Run a 2-week beta at 5 enterprises connecting their scanners and measure time-to-fix on a sample of findings.
riskiest_assumption.success_signal: Median time to remediate falls by 30%+ for the sample and 2 beta customers ask for a paid contract.

open_questions: Who owns remediation budget: security or IT?
How much automated fixing will customers allow?
